framework.notes:
- **Steam achievements now pause automatically while any mod is enabled.**
  Some mods make rare achievements trivial to earn, and nobody wants a
  cheapened trophy on their profile by accident - so with at least one mod
  enabled, the game no longer unlocks achievements or counts progress toward
  them (captures, promotions, and the other lifetime stats stop ticking up
  too). Disable all your mods and everything works exactly as before. If you
  know what you're doing and want achievements anyway, type `achievements on`
  in the console (F10) - that lasts until you quit the game, and the next
  launch starts paused again. Plain `achievements` shows the current state.
  The first time something would have unlocked, the console tells you it was
  paused, so nothing disappears silently. One knock-on effect: the secret Sky
  board scheme unlocks by checking the "land 100 pieces" Steam achievement, so
  it can't newly unlock while achievements are paused - play a stretch unmodded
  (or use `achievements on`) and it unlocks as normal. A scheme you already
  earned is unaffected.

manager.notes:
- **See the actual gambits.** Mods that add gambits now show them the way
  the game does: the real sprite on a collection-style tile with a
  rarity-tinted halo and shop price tag, a hover card with the gambit's
  name, rarity capsule and description (in the game's own rarity colors and
  text markup, keyword colors included), and the game's hover wiggle. On
  a modpack's page a "gambits inside" shelf shows everything the pack puts
  in your runs; Browse cards and pack member rows carry mini tiles. The
  data comes from a new optional `gambits` field on registry entries, and
  sprites load straight from each mod's own repository.
- **Nicer notifications.** Toasts stopped piling up: repeats merge into a
  little bump, at most three show at once, each drains a timer bar, click
  dismisses, and exits collapse smoothly instead of popping.
- Gambit tiles are quiet by design - no background fill and light chrome,
  so every rarity's ray halo actually reads (epic's used to vanish into
  the old wine tile). Tooltips are opaque, always layer above neighboring
  cards, and nudge themselves inside the window instead of clipping at
  its edge.
- Instances tab badge counts instances, the prompt dialog got breathing
  room, pack-page buttons share a height, and modpacks no longer show a
  meaningless summed download count (per-mod counts remain).

mods.name: 'Point A' Manager
mods.author: Agent15
mods.summary: Library that remembers the tile each piece moved from, for other mods to build on.
mods.description: Not much to see on its own - install it because another mod asked for it. The game only remembers where a piece landed; this library tracks where it came from (for both player and enemy moves) and offers a helper to compute the distance and direction of the last move. Powers gambits like Recursion's and Sniper's.

mods.name: Better Collection
mods.author: Ben
mods.summary: Makes the gambit collection screen run smoothly.
mods.description:
The collection screen was drawing every card, button and arrow over itself up to 1250 times to fake a thick outline - the page arrows alone rebuilt as 7,500 shapes each, every time anything moved. This draws them twice instead: same look, a fraction of the cost. The run-info screen you open mid-run is built from the same pieces and gets the same treatment.

Prefer the chunkier outlines? Type 'collection outlines 4' in the console (F10) to put them back.

mods.name: Fall Guy
mods.author: Ben
mods.summary: Pieces about to fall are saved to the nearest free square, or the stash.
mods.description:
An Epic gambit for 8 coins. When the crumble takes a tile out from under one of your pieces, the piece does not die: it hops to the nearest intact empty square. If the whole board is out of squares it is dropped into your stash instead, ready to be placed again. Only when the stash is full too does the fall play out as vanilla wrote it.

Every fall is covered - there is no per-game limit. The buy-back graveyard is kept honest: a saved piece's booking is rolled back so a rescue is never also a free graveyard copy.

gambits.description: Pieces about to <color=§>FALL</color> are saved to the nearest free square, or the stash.

mods.name: Impatient Gambit
mods.author: Ben
mods.summary: Skip every stage straight to its boss, and earn 4x gold.
mods.description:
A Legendary gambit for 10 coins. Buy it and the next game is your current stage's boss; every stage after that goes straight to its own boss too, so a run collapses from 25 games to 5. All gold earned is multiplied by 4 to keep that survivable - five payouts instead of twenty-five - and the win screen gains a fourth breakdown row showing the bonus.

The run's opening game is never skipped: vanilla never treats it as a boss fight either.

All gold earned is x4.

modpacks.name: Gambit Variety Pack
modpacks.author: Ben
modpacks.summary: Six community gambits in one click - a bit of rescue, a bit of chaos, a bit of greed.
modpacks.description:
A starter spread of custom gambits that play nicely together: Fall Guy rescues pieces from crumbling tiles, Kamikaze trades your piece for its killer, Spikes turns TRAP tiles lethal, GrandMa's Cookies hands you a free piece at the start, Lobbyist makes selling kings profitable, and Fishing Net freezes the enemy's turn when you trap someone.

The Gambit Creation API library installs automatically - it's the plumbing all of these are built on.
